definition: A library of individually-saved, named, thumbnailed POSES (not full captured motions) — organized into named categories such as defaults (A-Pose, Idle A/B, Confident/Relaxed/T-Pose), action (Fight Stance, Hit Reaction, Punch Anticipation/Contact/Follow Through, Kick A/B, Knockdown), and named cycles (Walk Cycle A/B, Run Cycle) — that can be dropped onto any frame of any rig to assemble a full cycle by chaining a handful of library poses, rather than hand-posing each key from scratch every time.
purpose: Turn animation authoring from 'pose everything by hand every time' into 'assemble a sequence from a reusable vocabulary of named poses', reducing a full idle cycle to selecting two or three library assets rather than keying a rig from a neutral pose each time.
visible_effect: A demonstrated idle cycle (Idle A at frame 0, Idle B at the cycle's midpoint) is assembled in seconds by double-clicking two library thumbnails onto two timeline positions, versus keying every joint by hand.
psychological_or_gameplay_effect: The source's own direct claim, demonstrated on camera: 'I've literally made an idle cycle in like 4 seconds' — the time saving is the whole point, not a secondary benefit.
physical_interpretation: None — an authoring-workflow structure, not a physical claim.
use_cases: rapidly assembling a first-pass idle, walk, or run cycle from named starting poses rather than keying from a neutral rest pose each time
consistent named acting/action poses (a fight stance, a hit reaction, a punch's anticipation/contact/follow-through beats) reused across many different characters or sequences
quickly generating thumbnail/showcase poses for non-animation purposes (the source's own example: using a library pose for a video thumbnail)
non_use_cases: a performance needing a genuinely unique, bespoke pose no library entry approximates — the library speeds up the COMMON case, it doesn't replace hand-posing for a novel one
final, polished character acting where a library pose is only ever a starting point requiring further refinement, not a finished result on its own
interactions: the master directive's open starting-recipe question (`project_cadence_animation_intelligence` memory, prompt §7.3) — this is the single most direct, concrete, evidenced real-world example this whole batch has found of exactly the kind of named-pose starting-recipe library that open question is about, complete with a working category taxonomy (defaults / action / cycles) and a demonstrated multi-second assembly workflow

the twelve-action-phase vocabulary already implicit in `authorMotion` (anticipation, key poses, breakdowns, holds, settle) — the library's own category names (Punch Anticipation, Punch Contact, Punch Follow Through) independently converge on the SAME phase vocabulary this build already uses internally, evidence that the phase model is a natural fit for a pose-library taxonomy

obari_punch_camera_facing_pose_sequence (video 62, this batch) — another concrete named-pose-sequence candidate; between the two, this batch now has multiple independent, evidenced examples supporting the same open design question
cadence_representation: Directly relevant to the still-open starting-recipe question and to `ai/library.js`'s existing cross-project motion library: that module already stores full captured/authored MOTIONS with a Part 36 profile; this entry's evidence is for a library of individual POSES (single points in time, not motion sequences) as a separate, smaller, faster-to-assemble unit one level below a full library entry. Neither `author_motion`'s PoseSpec-per-phase mechanism nor `ai/library.js` currently distinguishes a reusable named POSE from a reusable named MOTION — this entry is evidence that both units are independently useful and demanded in practice.
control_surface: `compile_pose`/`author_motion` can already take a PoseSpec per phase; no tool currently stores, names, thumbnails, or retrieves an individual reusable PoseSpec the way this source's library does.
detection_and_measurement_methods: Not directly measurable — an authoring-time convenience structure, not a property of finished motion data. Once assembled, the resulting cycle is measured by whatever existing checks already apply to a cycle (`keyDensity`, cross-repeat variance, etc.).
generation_or_modification_methods: None currently stores or retrieves named individual poses; `author_motion` authors a full phase sequence per call rather than dropping a single named pose onto an arbitrary frame.
failure_modes: treating a library pose as a finished result rather than a starting point needing further refinement for the specific shot
a category taxonomy that doesn't match the target rig's own phase/action vocabulary, making retrieval harder than hand-posing would have been
roblox_considerations: Directly reachable in a Roblox/Studio-adjacent tool as a per-user or per-project stored set of named `Pose`-equivalent snapshots (a joint-angle dictionary per named pose), retrievable and droppable onto any frame of any compatible R15/R6 rig.
performance_implications: An authoring-time saving only (fewer manual keying actions); no runtime cost implication once a cycle is assembled and baked to ordinary keyframes.
